text:
olivia: noticed a weird spike in client-side 429s during our nightly token refresh test. not the Retry-After header, just raw 429s.
tariq: did the clients use the sample-app or their own integration?
olivia: sample-app; we used the node quickstart that ships with the SDK. it retries immediate exponential w/o jitter.
sre-bot: alert: 02:12 UTC burst: 900 simultaneous reconnects -> connection pool exhaustion on api-gateway -> 200s p95 latency increase.
kevin: hmm. I think two things are colliding: token refresh causes many processes to re-auth at the same instant, and our SDK backoff is deterministic. we should switch to decorrelated jitter (a la full jitter) by default.
lina: quick primer: full jitter = sleep = rand(0, base * 2**attempt) which avoids synchronization better than +/- jitter on top of fixed backoff
maya: agree. also add a randomized per-process offset on startup (0-3s) to reduce alignment for long-running services.
olivia: sample-app lives in devex/samples. I can patch it. but we need parity across SDKs (python/go/node).
sdk-bot: note: current SDK releases -> node v1.3.3 (fixed exp), python v1.3.2 (full jitter opt-in), go v1.2.9 (no jitter).
tariq: we should standardize env var names: REDWOOD_RETRY_STRATEGY=(fixed|full-jitter|equal-jitter) and REDWOOD_RETRY_JITTER=0.3 for opt tuning.
kevin: another angle: connection pools. If many clients reuse the same http.Agent and retry simultaneously, pool queueing causes 502s/backpressure. SDK should jitter per-connection attempt, not just per-request.
maya: ops suggestion: add a client-side circuit-breaker that trips after N 429s in M seconds and exposes a short cooling period with exponential ramp down. prevents hot loops.
lina: for streaming customers, idempotency keys are tricky. propose: non-streaming requests get idempotency-key header by default (generated per-call unless user supplies), streaming gets a stream-id + resume-offset token from runtime to resume without replay.
olivia: runtime change will be needed. request: eng-runtime to provide resume_token in stream-close events and accept resume_token on new stream open.
sre-bot: telemetry idea: emit "client_retry_correlation" metric tag when bursts align with token-rotation events.
kevin: reproducible script idea: spawn N processes, each with M connections to the SDK, force token expiry, then let them refresh. I hacked one in bash and saw a spike. will upload gist.
tariq: tests: add a flaky e2e that asserts variance in retry times (stddev > threshold) to avoid deterministic retry shape. also unit tests for parse of Retry-After (s handles both seconds and HTTP date).
maya: we should treat absent Retry-After as "long, unknown" and apply full-jitter with a higher cap rather than immediate fast retry. set a minimum backoff base to 250ms.
olivia: for onboarding sample-app, add an interactive token-rotate mode and a small dashboard that shows per-client jitter distribution so customers can see the effect.
kevin: ops change: add server-side header X-Rate-Limit-Source to help correlate which frontends are hitting limiter. also add missing_retry_after_count metric.
ops-bot: deploy plan queued: canary sdk-node v1.3.4-jitter to 3% @ 18:00 UTC, python/go follow 6h later.
sdk-bot: PR checklist: changelog, env var docs, unit tests, integration flaky test, semver minor bump.
tariq: open question: should we automatically switch to cheaper fallback model when Retry-After > 10s? that's opinionated. maybe expose routing policy defaults and let customers opt-in.
kevin: agree opt-in. but default behavior could suggest fallback in console UI for customers on Dedicated.
olivia: action items: kevin (proof-of-concept full-jitter impl in node sdk), tariq (test harness + stddev assertion), maya (circuit-breaker spec), eng-runtime (resume token contract), ops (metrics), devex (sample-app updates + onboarding doc). I'll collect gists and link in a follow-up. thanks :raised_hands:
